scope: Independent read-only source and retained authoritative-reference research. No new native execution, repository-module import, builds, process queries/signals, simulator operation, application edits, or protection waiver. This additive report was explicitly authorized by root.
observations: Actual app09 boot1/save failed the required NSFileManager directory protection equality. Dictionary present, key absent, no NSError. Diagnostic-only file getter also lacked the key; both volume queries returned supported. Later original required checks did not execute. This was a test assertion failure, not an established application crash.

Actual Foundation02 uses attested control03 producer a6b025d7b77c3b1b1de57b93869d0beff6b4cc9e365eb5672ffd2be9d52013f2 (not the earlier similarly named control02 source). Direct Objective-C NSFileManager/NSData methods run in an arm64 iOS26.5 Simulator CLI, app_container=false. Native Foundation UUID 2cc9fce0-08f9-3a0d-8a2f-6db229462de5 is observed, not matched to a public source build.

Eight native operations return true without NSError/exception. Eight checkpoints all omit NSFileProtectionKey. Regular-file URL class reads return until-first-authentication, even after Atomic|Complete, direct Complete, and explicit FileManager Complete setter. Backup exclusion changes from included to excluded; containing-volume support remains true.

Production directory creation requests NSFileProtectionComplete; production writes encrypt first and use NSDataWritingAtomic OR NSDataWritingFileProtectionComplete, then exclude the result from backup. Requesting named flags and native success do not prove retained class or device enforcement.

classification_and_counter_evidence.claim: An application storage/Kotlin bridge bug explains the missing protection key.
classification_and_counter_evidence.reason: Independent direct Objective-C control reproduces absence before and after backup/settings; production requests the expected flags. Actual app-container native control has not run.

classification_and_counter_evidence.claim: Missing NSFileProtectionKey proves unsupported volume, plaintext snapshots, or missing entitlement.
classification_and_counter_evidence.reason: Volume capability is observed true; application encryption and OS Data Protection are distinct. No entitlement cause has been established. Do not add entitlements or weaken storage.

classification_and_counter_evidence.claim: Exact installed Simulator intentionally omits FileManager protection metadata.
classification_and_counter_evidence.reason: Official immutable source explicitly does so and actual native CLI observations agree, but the public commit has not been bound to installed Foundation UUID. This does not negate the measured absence.

classification_and_counter_evidence.claim: Strict Complete metadata expectation is inherently physical-only.
classification_and_counter_evidence.reason: Metadata reads are locally observable; this Simulator returns absent/non-Complete. No inspected authoritative API contract guarantees this Simulator will return Complete. Keep the original required gate FAIL/unresolved rather than auto-waiving it.

classification_and_counter_evidence.claim: Lock-state/keybag protection enforcement can be proved by functional Simulator saves.
classification_and_counter_evidence.reason: Actual iOS hardware/device lock behavior and backup protection require physical-device evidence, separate from metadata readback and encrypted-envelope functionality.
